Thinking a longer ramp is harder because it is longer. The path is longer, but each step of the push is easier.
Movers push heavy boxes up a ramp into a truck instead of lifting them straight up. The ramp is an inclined plane.

An inclined plane (ramp) lets you raise a load with a smaller push, but along a longer path. A wedge is two ramps back to back: it splits or cuts (an ax, a knife, a doorstop). A screw is a ramp wrapped around a post.
A ramp, a wedge and a screw.

Lifting a box 1 meter straight up takes a big force over a short path. Pushing it up a 4-meter ramp to the same height takes about a quarter of the force (plus a bit for friction), over four times the path.
Ramp A is 2 meters long, ramp B is 6 meters long. Both reach the same truck. Which needs less push?
Ramp B, the longer one, needs less push.
Both raise the box the same height.
The longer ramp spreads the work over a longer path.
Mountain roads zig-zag for the same reason: a longer, gentler path is easier to climb. A jar lid and a corkscrew are screws.
Thinking the longer ramp is harder because it is longer. Each step is easier; there are just more of them.
Going further. Simple Machines in Physical Science explains the numbers. To build a chain of ramps, a wedge and a screw lift yourself, try the Contraption Workshop.
